newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: PM SHRUGS OFF POLICE UNION CALLS FOR COLSTON INVESTIGATION
The Prime Minister's office has described as "a bit rich" the Federal Police Association's call for him to hand over the travel rort allegations against Senator Mal Colston for investigation.
The Association says it's time politicians accepted the public wants answers, warning there'll never be any public confidence until there's a police investigation.

Mr Howard's office says it's a bit rich for the police union to be complaining when it took nine months for them to complete an investigation into National Party MP, Michael Cobb, and former Liberal Senator Bob Woods.
A spokesman for the Prime Minister says the Police Association comments are not an official complaint from law enforcers.
PHAR LAP'S PROPOSED CASINO MOVE CONDEMNED
Gerry Telford, the son of Phar Lap's original trainer, has condemned a proposal to move the legendary race horse exhibit from the Museum of Victoria to Melbourne's Crown Casino.
Mr Telford, who was six when his father Harry donated the horse to the museum, says Phar Lap belongs to the people of Australia and never should be used as a commercial venture.
The casino wants to house the exhibit when the museum closes for renovations for two years in July.
The Victoria Racing Club says the move would be outrageous as those too young for the casino would be robbed of a piece of Australian folklore.
Bankcard managment says banks have neglected the old faithful plastic card in recent years in favour of newer products.
Bankcard's manager of operations, Gary Moffat, says the board of management will be meeting next month to consider the future of the credit card.
The two-decade old Bankcard has been under increasing pressure from heavy promotions of Visa and Master cards, as well as the emergence of the new value-added loyalty programmes.
The options range from closing it down, to revamping it with new chip technology and a promotional campaign.
QUEENSLAND APPROACH TO UNDERPAID ABORIGINES WELCOMED
The Federal Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission has welcomed the Queensland Government's attempt to correct past underpayment of Aborigines.
But Race Commissioner, Zita Antonios, says new evidence suggests it may be a more widespread problem.
She says recent inquiries have uncovered a raft of allegations dealing with the underpayment and non-payment of Aboriginal workers.
